takeaways: Treasury yields hit 24-year highs (10-year about 5.35%, 30-year 5.72%) with markets pricing about 85% odds of a December Fed hike, pushing buyers to re-trade CRE deals.

Private capital keeps consolidating senior living: BDT & MSD Partners are acquiring Sunrise Senior Living and CareTrust added a 45-property U.K. SHOP deal, while occupancy has risen 19 straight quarters on the thinnest supply pipeline since 2012.
Tishman Speyer closed the $235M Chrysler Building ground lease, and proptech raised $2.21B in Q3 led by EliseAI's $350M Series F, with AI capital concentrating in a few winners.

items.headline: Treasury yields hit 24-year highs as 10-year tests 5.35%
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury touched about 5.35% and the 30-year 5.72% on Oct 7, both 24-year highs, with the 10-year up 60+ bps since July on fiscal and inflation worries. Markets price roughly 85% odds of a December Fed hike, raising refinancing and cap-rate pressure for senior housing owners.

items.headline: Tishman Speyer closes $235M Chrysler Building ground lease with Cooper Union
items.summary: Tishman Speyer closed on the 150-year leasehold for the Chrysler Building at $235M including expected redevelopment costs, with PSP (about $225B AUM) as main equity partner. The Promote cautions against comparing it to the old $41M ground rent, as this is a wholly new structure. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Rising rates put CRE deals back on the negotiating table
items.summary: As yields climb, buyers are renegotiating pricing on deals that no longer pencil at agreed prices. Expect more re-trades and slower closings on senior housing acquisitions that rely on floating-rate or near-term financing.

items.headline: BDT & MSD Partners to acquire Sunrise Senior Living
items.summary: Investment group BDT & MSD Partners is acquiring Sunrise Senior Living, which plans to double down on luxury, bespoke resident experiences under new ownership. Another sign of large-scale private capital consolidating premium senior living operators.

items.headline: Proptech raised $2.21B in Q3; EliseAI leads with $350M Series F
items.summary: Seven largest deals took about 58% of funding. EliseAI's $350M Series F (about $742M total) led, followed by Kahua ($250M) and Invenergy ($215M). EliseAI's leasing automation is relevant to senior living sales and resident communication.

items.headline: CareTrust grows U.K. SHOP platform with 45-property care home deal
items.summary: CareTrust REIT expanded its U.K. senior housing operating platform through a 45-property care home acquisition, extending the REIT shift toward operator-aligned SHOP structures.

items.headline: SlateView closes second acquisition; BWE secures $28.3M loan
items.summary: SlateView Capital closed its second senior living acquisition and BWE secured a $28.3M loan, showing lenders and buyers remain active in the sector despite higher rates.

items.headline: Senior living occupancy has risen 19 straight quarters on thin new supply
items.summary: NIC MAP data showed occupancy at 89.5% in Q1 2026 (19th consecutive quarterly gain), with units under construction at their lowest since 2012 and inventory growth at a record low. Constrained supply supports occupancy for existing communities.

items.headline: Activist Erez takes 5.8% stake in Empire State Realty Trust
items.summary: Activist investor Erez disclosed a 5.8% stake in Empire State Realty Trust, signaling pressure on public CRE owners to unlock value as rates rise.

items.headline: Newmark shops H&M's Fifth Ave flagship leasehold at 589 Fifth
items.summary: The 184K sf leasehold (68K sf retail) is in play; Macquarie's GLL signed a $365M 99-year ground lease with the Mactaggart family in 2019. Guidance TBD. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Oracle tells Blue Owl it may not pay rent on data center leases
items.summary: The Promote flags a force majeure dispute in which Oracle is signaling reluctance to pay rent to Blue Owl on capital-intensive data center assets, highlighting tenant-credit risk in the AI buildout. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Nvidia retains staff with flat structure and two extra days off each quarter
items.summary: Nvidia avoids org charts and gives employees two additional days off every quarter, a retention approach worth noting for operators fighting turnover.

items.headline: '3 Jobs in One': how 8 operators support and train executive directors
items.summary: Eight senior living operators describe how they hire, train and support executive directors, a role central to community performance and retention.

items.headline: Sleep under 7 hours linked to lower life expectancy, second only to smoking
items.summary: An OHSU study in Sleep Advances found insufficient sleep (<7 hours) was still associated with shorter life expectancy after adjusting for inactivity, employment and education; only smoking was a stronger link. The study is observational.

items.headline: Rural senior living operators lean on reputation to stand out
items.summary: Operators in smaller markets are differentiating through local reputation and community ties rather than amenity spend, a playbook relevant to non-primary-market communities.

items.headline: Manhattan new development contracts fall to 240 in Q3
items.summary: Contracts for new Manhattan development units fell to 240 in Q3, a sign higher rates and uncertainty are weighing on luxury residential demand.

items.headline: Inside Real Estate adds Cotality data to AI platform Streams
items.summary: Cotality property data, including buyer/seller propensity scores and ownership history, is being added to Streams for select teams, with broader access expected in coming months.

items.headline: Standard Chartered tackles banking's class problem
items.summary: Standard Chartered says 'where you come from shouldn't dictate where you finish,' with CFO Darren Ellis describing efforts to widen advancement paths.

items.headline: Wealthy Gen Zers quietly outspend boomers and millennials on art
items.summary: Fortune reports wealthy Gen Z collectors are outspending older cohorts on art while keeping collections off social media.

items.headline: Ken Griffin's Carnegie Mellon Miami gift headlines The Promote pod
items.summary: This week's pod calls the Griffin/CMU Miami deal arguably the CRE deal of the year, centered on Moishe Mana's Wynwood assemblage exit; also covers Bain's rescue recap talks for Hong Kong's New World. (via The Promote)
